findings.summary: verify_snapshot rejects every producer-generated bundle rather than proving archive/manifest replay.
findings.evidence: The producer's manifest entries contain kind, resolvedTargetPath, and symlinkTarget (lines 618-631), but verify_snapshot constructs archive_metadata with only path, sha256, size, mode, and state (lines 1062-1065) and compares those unequal objects at line 1066. The normal successful replay path is untested; the tampering test only observes a rejection.
findings.impact: The required archive-replay proof cannot be obtained from the produced artifact, so the snapshot cannot serve as integrity evidence.
findings.required_remediation: Make manifest/archive metadata comparison exact and schema-aware, add a passing verification test for an untouched bundle, and retain tampering tests.

findings.summary: Pre/post checks do not hash the scanner-input denominator and miss content drift within an already-dirty tracked file.
findings.evidence: Descriptors and their bytes are collected before pre-state capture (lines 924-934). The subsequent comparison only checks porcelain/status and staged-diff hashes (lines 938-945). Mutating a tracked file that was already unstaged-modified between those captures leaves both status and staged diff unchanged, while the accepted scan can consume different bytes from the archived manifest.
findings.impact: This violates FR2's required immediate pre/post complete-denominator hash and permits an unbound dirty-worktree scan.
findings.required_remediation: Re-discover and hash the full denominator immediately before and after the scan boundary, compare paths, metadata, and bytes, and add an adversarial test that changes an already-dirty tracked TypeScript input.

findings.summary: The advertised R0 projection is not consumable by the accepted R0 validator.
findings.evidence: The producer emits schemaVersion 2 and archive entries with kind/symlink fields (lines 32, 637-650, 793-800). The unchanged accepted R0 validator requires archive schemaVersion 1 and exactly contentBase64/mode/path/sha256/size/state entry keys (measure/business_operations_graph_baseline_validation.py lines 433-466). The only integration test validates static v1 fixtures, not a produced source_snapshot/candidate.
findings.impact: A real R1 artifact cannot be validated through the accepted R0 boundary, contrary to the claimed R0 integration and the required fail-closed evidence chain.
findings.required_remediation: Either produce the accepted v1 artifact contract or version and independently accept a compatible validator contract; add an end-to-end produced-artifact validation test without weakening R0.

findings.summary: The source denominator is incomplete for nested tsconfig extends chains and staged deletions.
findings.evidence: Only files whose names match tsconfig*.json are parsed into configs (lines 443-447). A direct extended config such as config/base.json is added as a descriptor later (lines 464-482) but never parsed, so its own extends target is not discovered. Separately, deleted inputs come only from git ls-files --deleted (lines 178-181 and 487-503); a staged deletion has already been removed from the index and is not covered, despite staged status being separately observed.
findings.impact: The producer can omit scanner-relevant configuration or deleted TypeScript inputs, defeating the complete denominator required by FR2.
findings.required_remediation: Resolve and parse every reachable in-repository extends target recursively (including safe symlinked configs where supported), union staged and unstaged deletions, and test nested extends plus staged deletion cases.

findings.summary: The master-branch invariant is not actually enforced and regular-file modes are fabricated.
findings.evidence: _git_worktree_state hard-codes branch: master rather than reading Git (lines 210-219), so _check_worktree_state's branch check (lines 222-233) always passes. Regular descriptors set mode to 100644 without inspecting stat data (lines 451-463 and 471-482), losing executable metadata required by FR2.
findings.impact: The producer may create evidence from another branch while labeling it master and cannot faithfully reproduce required path metadata.
findings.required_remediation: Read and require the actual symbolic branch, validate the supplied scanner root is the sole worktree root, capture lstat-derived modes, and add non-master and executable-input rejection/fidelity tests.

positive_observations: The focused tests exercise tracked and untracked inputs, an unstaged deletion, a simple symlink, path traversal/duplication rejection, and a visible-status drift case.
Producer Git invocations shown in the reviewed implementation are read-only; no reviewed command stages, resets, stashes, or otherwise writes the real index.
